clue.text: To defend it could be all on West

indicators.note: the clue suggests these letters could be something else once rearranged, flagging an anagram

explanation.surface: A general muses that holding his position might mean putting everything on the western flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals that ALL ON WEST is rearranged; 'it' is a link. In cricket a batsman who stonewalls blocks every ball rather than scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstinate blocking, whether by a batsman or a politician refusing questions, so it is a dogged kind of resistance.

clue.text: No holds barred for this workman?

definitions.text: No holds barred for this workman?

parts.words: No holds barred for this workman?
parts.note: the wrestling phrase 'no holds barred' is reread literally: this dock labourer is never kept out of a ship's cargo holds

explanation.surface: A wrestler who will try any grip at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker who loads and unloads cargo from ships' holds works in every hold there is.

clue.text: Antennae coil showing main element reversed

indicators.note: the run picked out is read backwards, from right to left
the letters are on show inside the words antennae coil, signalling a run picked from them

explanation.surface: A radio aerial's coil reveals some chemical element when turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' picks NAECO from antenNAE COil and 'reversed' turns it round. 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the high seas, and the sea is one of the classical elements of nature.

clue.text: Disappear from the East Virginia scene perhaps

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: the word scene is offered tentatively, so its letters may appear in another order

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes from the eastern Virginia locale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SCENE into NESCE, placed after E and VA; 'from the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to fade away like vapour, a literary verb for vanishing gradually.

clue.text: ---- should be made of sterner stuff" (J Caesar)

definitions.text: ---- should be made of sterner stuff" (J Caesar)

parts.words: should be made of sterner stuff" (J Caesar)
parts.note: fill in the missing opening word of Mark Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's play about Caesar

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its first word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar Mark Antony says Caesar wept for the poor, and that the quality Brutus accused him of should be made of sterner stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the desire to rise and gain power that Brutus charged Caesar with.

clue.text: Call on to view the sky at night

definitions.meaning: to pay a visit to someone, as when passing through their town

definitions.text: to view the sky at night
definitions.meaning: to raise one's eyes towards the stars overhead

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are phrasal: visiting an acquaintance, and literally directing your gaze upward to the heavens.

clue.text: Exception to no man being an island

definitions.text: Exception to no man being an island

parts.words: Exception to no man being an island
parts.note: Donne wrote that no man is an island; here an archaic word for a man is also the name of an island off southern England

explanation.surface: A rebuttal of John Donne's famous line about human connection.
explanation.walkthrough: A wight is an old word for a person, and the Isle of Wight lies off England's south coast, so this man is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a human being doubles as the name of an English island, contradicting Donne.

clue.text: Fuller figure for a notability

definitions.meaning: Thomas Fuller wrote The History of the Worthies of England, profiles of famous people
a person of note or distinction

explanation.surface: A plumper shape suited to a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuller' is not about size: it is the 17th-century writer Thomas Fuller, whose book profiled England's eminent people.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent, distinguished person is called this, and Fuller's subjects were exactly such people.

clue.text: Took a chance say and danced for joy

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like the one to be written

parts.note: to take a chance is to gamble, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone risked a bet and then jigged about in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that the word for 'took a chance' sounds the same as the answer; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and frolic playfully, like lambs in spring.

clue.text: This saw return of a musical group

indicators.note: return means the group's name is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a nonet is an ensemble of nine musicians

explanation.surface: This person witnessed a band coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns NONET round. 'saw' is not the verb but the noun: a tenon saw is a fine-toothed carpentry saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small stiff-backed handsaw used for cutting joints in woodwork.

clue.text: We take blame swapping valued possession

indicators.note: the letters swap places, so the words we and blame are rearranged

explanation.surface: We accept the blame by changing places with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping' rearranges WE plus BLAME; 'take' is a link. In the Bible the prophet Nathan tells of a poor man whose one cherished ewe lamb is taken by a rich man.
explanation.definitionFit: From Nathan's parable, a ewe lamb is a person's single most treasured possession.

clue.text: Kind of propeller functioning back to front

definitions.text: Kind of propeller functioning back to front

parts.words: Kind of propeller functioning back to front
parts.note: a person who drives a boat along while facing the stern, so working backwards

explanation.surface: A ship's screw that has been fitted the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'propeller' suggests a ship's screw, but this one is a person: a rower faces backwards while moving the boat forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower pulls the blades while seated facing the stern, so propels the boat while looking backwards.

clue.text: Selector whose word you hope is your bond

definitions.text: Selector whose word you hope is your bond

parts.words: Selector whose word you hope is your bond
parts.note: the machine that draws winning numbers for British Premium Bonds; you hope its choice is your bond number

explanation.surface: A judge whose promise you trust, playing on 'my word is my bond'.
explanation.walkthrough: The British savings scheme Premium Bonds pays prizes by lottery, the winning numbers picked by a computer with this acronym name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment chooses the winning Premium Bond numbers each month.

clue.text: Land or handle a bit of fluff

parts.note: to handle something is to touch it
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: Either come in to land or stroke a little fluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft lands when its wheels meet the runway, the moment of touching the ground.

clue.text: Protester finds nothing right with design

parts.note: a design is an aim or purpose, an object
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A demonstrator discovers nothing correct about the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in answer order, design first; 'finds' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises objections, such as a conscientious refuser of military service, is one who protests.

clue.text: Air transport — in the Black Forest?

parts.note: jet is a deep black mineral, so jet-black
planes are trees, so a forest of them

explanation.surface: Flying over Germany's Black Forest region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Forest' looks like the German region, but it splits: black is JET and a forest is made of plane trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet-propelled aircraft carry people and freight through the skies.

clue.text: Type of staff to tire

definitions.meaning: a flagstaff is a pole for a banner

explanation.surface: A kind of pole for wearying people.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner flies from a flagstaff, and as a verb to flag means to droop with weariness.

clue.text: Prime material for a plot

parts.note: the explosive that primes a charge, and the substance behind the 1605 conspiracy of Guy Fawkes

explanation.surface: The essential ingredient for a story's storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a novel, but this is the Catholic conspiracy of 1605 to blow up Parliament, remembered on Bonfire Night in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Black powder was the explosive stacked under Parliament by Fawkes and his fellow conspirators.

clue.text: Volcanic vent creates difficulty for a mule

indicators.note: making trouble for the words for a mule churns their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A steaming crack in volcanic ground makes trouble for a pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates difficulty' rearranges FOR A MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumarole is an opening near a volcano from which hot gases and steam escape.

clue.text: Monotony — no sign of, the monster

definitions.text: Monotony — no sign of, the monster

parts.words: Monotony — no sign of, the monster
parts.note: a still, calm Scottish loch without ripples shows no sign of its famous monster, giving a word for dull sameness

explanation.surface: Boredom at Loch Ness when the monster fails to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Loch Ness Monster, Nessie, is said to live in Loch Ness in Scotland; when the water is calm, with nothing stirring, it is flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull sameness with nothing rising or falling is a lack of variation, like a flat calm.

clue.text: What one does to this grub

definitions.meaning: the action one performs on food

explanation.definitionFit: Food is consumed, and the slang noun for food is a plural of the same verb.

clue.text: Pick out and destroy, done maybe in battle

parts.note: to cull is to select and kill animals

indicators.note: maybe means the word done is only one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to choose and kill something, finished perhaps during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges DONE into ODEN, after CULL; 'in' is a link. Culloden (1746) in Scotland was the last pitched battle on British soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1746 defeat of the Jacobite army near Inverness is known by this place name.

clue.text: Climbs — up or down the staff?

definitions.meaning: musical runs of notes rising or falling on the stave

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a pole, up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave of five lines; scales run up and down it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall is to ascend it, and musicians practise runs of notes ascending and descending the stave.

clue.text: Root of persuasion

parts.note: an orange root vegetable, also the reward dangled before a donkey to coax it

explanation.surface: The fundamental basis of persuading someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' looks like 'origin', but it is literal: the vegetable used as an incentive in 'carrot and stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticing reward is offered as an inducement, the opposite of the stick, and the vegetable is a root.

clue.text: Cold in the head? A remedy from the Crimea

definitions.text: Cold in the head? A remedy from the Crimea

parts.words: Cold in the head? A remedy from the Crimea
parts.note: a knitted head covering that keeps the head warm, named after a Crimean War battle

explanation.surface: Advice for treating a head cold with a Crimean folk cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold in the head' suggests catching a chill, but the remedy is a woollen hood worn by soldiers in the Crimean War of the 1850s, named after the battle site.
explanation.definitionFit: This woollen helmet covering the head and neck was worn by British troops in the Crimea against the cold.

clue.text: Grass cutter

definitions.meaning: the sharp edge of a knife

explanation.surface: A lawnmower.
explanation.definitionFit: One flat leaf of grass is a blade, and so is the cutting edge of a knife or sword.

clue.text: Time for issuing notes

parts.note: the speed at which musical notes are played, not the issuing of banknotes

explanation.surface: The moment for printing new banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests money from a bank, but these are musical ones; the pace at which they come out is the musical time.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the speed or pace of a piece is indicated by its Italian name for time.

clue.text: Girl of the month or first citizen

parts.note: May is a girl's name and also a month
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between a pin-up and the town's leading resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl of the month' looks like a pin-up, but it is a name that is also a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a town council is traditionally its first citizen, presiding over civic functions.

clue.text: Ring-shaped if with lunar formation

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if, as in Shakespeare

indicators.note: a formation of the word lunar arranges its letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something ring-shaped whether or not it formed on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges LUNAR into NULAR, after AN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Latin for a little ring, this describes anything shaped like a circle with a hole, such as an eclipse.

clue.text: Like Odin, a person observed

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should
eyed means watched or observed

explanation.surface: Someone noticed, resembling the Norse god.
explanation.walkthrough: Odin, chief of the Norse gods, gave up an eye to drink from the well of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin sacrificed an eye for wisdom, so the god has only a single eye.

clue.text: Stops losing head and relaxes

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost, as if beheaded

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Someone halts, falls apart and then calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the C from CEASES; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken or loosen, letting tension go.

clue.text: Roget for instance, such a man of words?

definitions.text: Roget for instance, such a man of words?

parts.words: Roget for instance, such a man of words?
parts.note: Roget compiled a thesaurus, a Greek word for treasury, so he keeps a store of words like a keeper of funds

explanation.surface: Peter Roget described as a wordsmith.
explanation.walkthrough: Thesaurus comes from the Greek for treasure-house, so the compiler of one is a keeper of a word treasury, a society's money-keeper in normal use.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who keeps a club's funds holds its treasury, and Roget held a treasury of words.
